questions.q: In 'The Fox and the Lion', what did the young Fox do the third time he saw the Lion?
choices: Walked boldly up and said hello
Ran to the nearest hiding place
Hid behind a tree to look
Climbed a tree to get away
questions.evidence: the third time, the Fox went boldly up to the Lion

questions.q: In 'The Lion and the Ass', what was the Ass's job in the hunt?
choices: To go into the cave and drive the Goats out
To stand at the cave entrance and keep watch
To follow the Goats' footprints in the dirt
To carry the Goats home to the Lion's den
questions.evidence: The Ass was to go into the cave and drive the Goats out

questions.q: In 'The Lion and the Ass', why was the Lion not scared by the Ass's noise?
choices: He knew the Ass and his kind
He could not hear inside the cave
He was too busy eating Goats
He had fallen asleep outside
questions.evidence: if I had not known you and your kind I should certainly have run, too

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Lion and the Ass'?
choices: A loud boaster does not impress people who know him
Hunting is much easier when you have a friend along
Always share what you catch with those who helped
Goats should never try to hide inside a dark cave
questions.evidence: The loud-mouthed boaster does not impress nor frighten those who know him.

questions.q: In 'The Dog and His Master's Dinner', what was the Dog's mistake?
choices: He stopped to argue with the other Dogs
He ate the dinner on the way to his master
He took the wrong road and got lost
He forgot the basket at the butcher's shop
questions.evidence: But at last he stopped to argue.

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Dog and His Master's Dinner'?
choices: Do not stop to argue with temptation
Always share your food with friends
Dogs make good helpers for masters
Run as fast as you can on errands
questions.evidence: Do not stop to argue with temptation.

questions.q: In 'The Vain Jackdaw and His Borrowed Feathers', what did the Jackdaw do to look like a Peacock?
choices: Stuck castoff Peacock feathers among his own
Painted his black feathers in bright colors
Asked the King of birds for new feathers
Ate special berries to grow a long tail
questions.evidence: he picked up some castoff feathers of the Peacocks and stuck them among his own black plumes

questions.q: In 'The Vain Jackdaw', why did the other Jackdaws drive him away when he came back?
choices: He had acted like he was better than them
They thought he was a Peacock come to visit
They had no food to share with a stranger
He had pecked them first when he came back
questions.evidence: They had not forgotten his superior airs toward them

questions.q: In 'The Monkey and the Dolphin', how did the Dolphin find out the Monkey was not a man?
choices: He called Piraeus a friend, but it is a port
The Monkey fell off his back into the sea
The Monkey started to chatter and squeak
Another Dolphin swam up and told him
questions.evidence: Piraeus is my very best friend.

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Monkey and the Dolphin'?
choices: One lie leads to another
Dolphins are friends to all
Never go to sea in a ship
Monkeys are good swimmers
